item.text: I’ll read the service documentation first, then retrieve the complete dataset with retries, token refreshes, rate-limit handling, and per-customer caching.

item.aggregated_output:
Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

item.text: The API has 50-order pages and separate customer records. I’m using integer half-up rounding per order, preserving every listed order ID globally so the duplicate count also includes non-qualifying repeats.
The full retrieval completed successfully despite the short-lived-token and rate-limit behavior. I’m doing a final structural check of the deliverable and reconciliation of the regional subtotal.

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('result.json')
data = json.loads(p.read_text())
expected = {'total_cents', 'order_count', 'duplicates_skipped', 'by_region'}
assert set(data) == expected
assert set(data['by_region']) == {'north', 'south', 'east', 'west'}
assert all(isinstance(v, int) for v in data['by_region'].values())
assert all(isinstance(data[k], int) for k in expected - {'by_region'})
assert sum(data['by_region'].values()) == data['total_cents']
print('validated', data['total_cents'], data['order_count'], data['duplicates_skipped'])
PY
rg --files -g '"'!*result.json'"'"
